extracted.intended_audience: Inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF) administrators, hospital finance officers, Medicare payment policy stakeholders, and commenters on CMS rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Defines the FY 2025 Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility Prospective Payment System (IRF PPS) payment update and related methodologies, including CMG relative weight updates, ALOS use, market basket and productivity adjustments, labor-related share calculation, and budget-neutral implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget neutrality factor application for CMG relative weight changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine a budget neutrality factor (Step 3: divide the amount calculated in Step 1 by the amount calculated in Step 2) and apply that budget neutrality factor to the FY 2025 IRF PPS standard payment amount after the application of the budget-neutral wage adjustment factor (Step 4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the calculation produced a budget neutrality factor of 0.9976. CMS implements CMG relative weight revisions in a budget-neutral manner so that total estimated aggregate payments to IRFs for FY 2025 are not affected; instead, the revisions affect distribution of payments within CMGs and tiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of CMG relative weights and ALOS table for case classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 2 presents CMGs, comorbidity tiers, corresponding relative weights, and average length of stay (ALOS) values for each CMG and tier for FY 2025; the ALOS for each CMG is used to determine when an IRF discharge meets the definition of a short stay transfer, which results in a per diem case-level adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS uses the ALOS per CMG to identify short stay transfers and apply per diem adjustments. Table 3 summarizes distributional effects (e.g., percent of cases with <5% change).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual update of CMG relative weights using most recent IRF cost data (HSRV method)
rubrics_metrics.description: The methodology to update CMG relative weights uses the most recent cost data reported by IRFs to compute relative weights that reflect the relative costliness of different IRF cases; the hospital-specific relative value (HSRV) method is used to assign payment weights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weights are empirically derived and proportional to the resources needed for an average case in that CMG. CMS updates CMG relative weights each year based on the full population of IRF Medicare fee-for-service beneficiaries. CMS did not propose changes to the HSRV method for FY 2025 and believes careful evaluation is required before moving to an average-cost weighting method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not manipulate relative weights to favor specific conditions; reflect reported costs
rubrics_metrics.description: CMG weights are derived entirely based on the data IRFs report on their claims and cost reports; CMS will not manipulate these data to increase certain relative weights (for example for the 13 qualifying conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS explains that the 13 qualifying conditions historically define IRF patient mix but are not necessarily more costly; weights should reflect empirically reported costs, not policy preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation of CMG weight revisions in a budget-neutral manner
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions to CMG relative weights are implemented budget-neutrally so total estimated aggregate payments remain the same for FY 2025; the revisions change distribution across CMGs and tiers without changing aggregate spending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distributional effects are reported (Table 3 shows most cases experience <5% change). The budget-neutral implementation requires applying a conversion factor (budget neutrality factor) to standard payments after wage adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory requirement to base IRF PPS update on market basket with productivity adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(j)(3)(C) of the Act requires the Secretary to establish an increase factor based on an appropriate percentage increase in a market basket of goods and services and to apply the productivity adjustment described in section 1886(b)(3)(B)(xi)(II) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS must update IRF PPS payments each FY by the market basket increase factor reduced by the statutory productivity adjustment. CMS states it does not have authority to apply a different update factor for FY 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of IGI (IHS Global Inc.) forecasts and most recent data for market basket update
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with historical practice, CMS estimates the market basket update for the IRF PPS based on IGI's forecasts using the most recent available data and will use more recent data if available and appropriate between proposed and final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example forecasts: IGI Q4 2023 projected a 2021-based IRF market basket increase of 3.2%; IGI Q2 2024 projected 3.5%. CMS uses the latest appropriate forecast when finalizing updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productivity adjustment methodology (10-year moving average of BLS TFP)
rubrics_metrics.description: The productivity adjustment is equal to the 10-year moving average of changes in annual economy-wide, private nonfarm business total factor productivity (TFP) as published by BLS; this adjustment reduces the market basket increase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BLS changed terminology from MFP to TFP with no data/method change. For FY 2025, IGI Q2 2024 projected a 10-year moving average TFP growth of 0.5 percent (used as the productivity adjustment), yielding a net update of 3.0 percent (3.5% - 0.5%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of the market basket as a fixed-weight Laspeyres index and rebasing rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: The IRF market basket is a fixed-weight, Laspeyres-type index that measures change in price over time of the same mix of goods and services purchased by IRFs in the base period; cost (price × quantity) changes are reflected only when the market basket is rebased to a more recent base year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS rebased the market basket to a 2021 base year (FY 2024) to better reflect current cost structures. The market basket inherently reflects price pressures prospectively but not quantity changes except via rebasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Employment Cost Index (ECI) for hospital wages as proxy for IRF compensation growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Because IRF-specific ECI information is unavailable, CMS uses the ECI for Wages and Salaries for All Civilian workers in Hospitals as the best available price proxy to account for compensation changes in the IRF market basket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS believes the hospital ECI reasonably captures the highly skilled workforce in IRFs (therapists, nurses, clinicians). IGI considers overall labor market conditions and contract labor trends when forecasting compensation price growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach to stakeholder comments on forecast errors and alternate adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS acknowledges concerns about forecast underestimation but explains there is no precedent to adjust IRF rates retrospectively for market basket forecast errors; forecast errors can be both positive and negative and cumulative errors since inception are small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS considered commenters' requests for one-time forecast error adjustments or alternative data sources but finalized a productivity-adjusted market basket increase of 3.0% for FY 2025 based on most recent data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor-related share calculation for wage index adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(j)(6) requires adjusting the proportion of IRF costs attributable to wages and wage-related costs; CMS proposed (and updated) the labor-related share by summing the relative importance of specified cost categories from the 2021-based IRF market basket and adding a labor-influenced portion of Capital-Related costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost categories included: Wages & Salaries; Employee Benefits; Professional Fees: Labor-Related; Administrative and Facilities Support Services; Installation, Maintenance, & Repair Services; All Other: Labor-Related Services. CMS used 46% as the portion of Capital-Related costs influenced by local labor markets and applied it to an 8.1% relative importance for Capital to derive a labor-related capital share of 3.7%. Based on IGI Q2 2024, the total labor-related share for FY 2025 was 74.4% (70.7% operating + 3.7% capital).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates for finalized CMG and ALOS updates
rubrics_metrics.description: The finalized updates to CMG relative weights and ALOS values are effective for FY 2025, for discharges occurring on or after October 1, 2024 and on or before September 30, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply revised CMG weights and ALOS values only to discharges within the FY 2025 period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory constraint: required application of productivity adjustment and limitation on CMS authority
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS is required by statute (section 1886(j)(3)(C)(ii)(I)) to apply the productivity adjustment and cannot suspend or modify it through rulemaking beyond statutory allowances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters requesting suspension or modification of the productivity adjustment were informed CMS lacks authority to eliminate the statutory productivity cut for FY 2025.
